newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada spot natural gas soars as cold continues.
newsitem.headline: Canada spot natural gas soars as cold continues.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices rocketed to year-high levels Wednesday, spurred by continuing frigid weather and a bull market across North America.

Gas at Alberta's AECO storage hub was quoted as high as C$2.75 per gigajoule, up from C$1.87 per GJ last week and C$2.15 on Tuesday. The story was similar for gas for delivery in all winter months. December AECO was talked at C$2.65/gigajoule, up from C$1.88 per on November 13.
Traders said the surge mostly thanks to forecasts for under -20 C (-4 F) weather in the west through the weekend.
Adding to the strength were high prices across the continent as fears heightened over low storage levels in the U.S. producing and western regions as well as a rising futures market.
Traders said the unusual strength in longer term pricing suggested there was little chance of prices easing in the near future.

In British Columbia, gas prices surged about US$1 per million British thermal units to US$4 on the day as Westcoast Energy's pipeline system cut deliveries to firm service only. Gas for export at Niagara, Ontario was discussed at US$3.80 per mmBtu, up 63 cents from last week. -- Reuters Calgary Bureau 403 531-1624
